overview: IAM is the global service that controls who can do what in an AWS account. People become users, users are organised into groups, and JSON policies attached to users or groups grant only the permissions they need.

coreConcepts.definition: Identity and Access Management: a global service for users, groups, roles and permissions.
Account created by default with full access; should not be used or shared.
An identity for one person in your organisation.
A collection of users; groups contain users only, never other groups.
A JSON document defining the permissions of the users or groups it is attached to.
A policy attached directly to a single user rather than inherited from a group.
Grant no more permissions than a user needs.

mustRemember: The root account is created by default and should not be used or shared.
Groups only contain users, not other groups.
A user can belong to no group or to multiple groups.
A user in several groups inherits the policies of all of them.
Policy structure: Version (always "2012-10-17"), optional Id, and one or more Statements.
Statement elements: optional Sid, Effect, Principal, Action, Resource, optional Condition.
Effect is either Allow or Deny.

keyComparisons.difference: Group policies apply to every member; an inline policy applies only to the one user it is attached to.
Action lists the API calls; Resource lists what those calls apply to.

commonMisunderstandings: Groups cannot be nested inside other groups.
Users do not have to belong to a group.
Least privilege does not mean granting broad access for convenience.
mentalModels: User = a person, group = a team, policy = the team's permission slip in JSON.
Read a statement as: Effect the Principal to do Action on Resource when Condition holds.
edgeCases: A user outside any group can still get permissions through an inline policy.

whenToUse.situation: Several people need the same permissions
whenToUse.use: Put them in a group and attach the policy to the group

whenToUse.situation: One user needs a one-off extra permission
whenToUse.use: An inline policy on that user

patternsToRecognize.signal: JSON with Effect, Action and Resource

examTraps.trap: Use the root account for daily administration
examTraps.correction: Create IAM users; reserve root for account setup.

examTraps.trap: A user can belong to only one group
examTraps.correction: Users can belong to multiple groups.

beyondSource: When Allow and an explicit Deny both apply to a request, the explicit Deny wins.
